outlook: Wheat kept sliding Friday while corn and soybeans bounced slightly. December Minneapolis spring wheat fell 4 cents to $6.16 (down 7¾ cents on the week) and December Chicago wheat lost 8 cents to $5.91¼, a four-month low, on technical selling that has had wheat trending lower since early September. January soybeans rose 5½ cents to $11.93¾ on late short covering after touching an 11-week low (still down 40½ cents on the week), and December corn gained 1½ cents to $4.41½ (down 6½ cents on the week); a sharp stock market sell-off and a stronger U.S. dollar weighed on grains this week. January canola eased C$1 to C$752.20 even as Canada and China extended their tariff agreement, and traders now turn to Tuesday's USDA WASDE report.
